full_judgment: 4. Mrs. Rabiya Bhuiyan, learned Advocate for the appellant has pointed out that the learned Single Judge himself observed that there was no error of law in the order of the lower appellate court "which can warrant any interference", and has contended that when the lower appellate court's order was found to be perfectly lawful the learned Single Judge fell into an error of law in allowing 7 months time to the tenant at fault enabling him to further delay the execution which was held up for about 8 years. The learned Advocate has rightly contended that even on a compassionate ground no time should have been allowed to the tenant without hearing the landlord, particularly by issuing a rule on the revisional application filed by the tenant-respondent. There is of course much substance in this contention of the learned Advocate, but as the time for 7 months is going to expire very soon the appeal itself has virtually become infructuous. Reversal of the impugned order will render the respondent's occupation of the premises during this period unauthorised without bringing any benefit to the appellant. The impugned order, in the circumstances, need not be set aside. The respondent must vacate the premises on the expiry of the period allowed by the learned Single Judge.
